title: Covering a hole is not yet an attachment
subtitle: Inspect three original patch plans.
summary: Inspect three original patch plans. Test coverage and layer presence as separate geometric questions, then identify the physical evidence still missing.
audience: General readers; all selected evidence and task instructions are included.
scope: Dimensionless plan analysis; no completed swatch, durability claim, practical handling instruction or observed reproduction. A non-sewing route supplies the whole task.

passages.title: Separate overlap and attachment
passages.text: The iFixit account discusses overlap, edge attachment and tension. The Sewing & Craft Alliance distinguishes temporary basting and restricts its seam example to work without strain. Neither source proves that the original plans below have been made or tested.

lenses.label: Compare covered area
lenses.observation: The hole has area 20 × 20 = 400 square units.
lenses.question: Which patch covers all of that rectangle?
readings: Through-layers and miss-base both cover 400; partial-cover covers 10 × 20 = 200.
Coverage alone cannot tell whether any proposed location passes through intact base fabric.
lenses.boundary: Drawing units are not material dimensions.

lenses.label: Read the missing base
lenses.observation: The miss-base plan places every marked point inside the hole.
lenses.question: Why can a patch cover the hole while its proposed locations miss the base?
readings: Patch material exists at those points, but the base has a hole there.
The other plans mark locations in both intended layers, even though partial-cover still leaves half the hole exposed.
lenses.boundary: A location predicate does not describe the whole thread path, fastening or tension.

lenses.label: Ask what a specimen could show
lenses.observation: All physical verdicts in the preparation packet are unfilled.
lenses.question: What would need observation before calling it a successful attachment?
readings: Inspect actual materials, fastening, missed layers and tension on both sides.
Record deviations and a reproducible inspection; later washing/load performance is a different claim.
lenses.boundary: No physical pass is inferred from a neat drawing or a correct calculation.

activity.transfer: Design a fourth rectangle-and-point plan that passes one drawing predicate but fails the other. Explain its coordinates, then name two physical properties your drawing still cannot establish.
rubric: Separate area coverage from layer presence.
Treat the hole as absent base fabric.
Distinguish a proposed location from a finished stitch.
Keep physical outcomes unknown until observed.
